title: Midnight capacity sprint — personal docket
body:
Late-shift brain dump / quick checklist (for Lena)

Context:
- Oncall night: follow up on pool imbalances, finish the mini rebin across n2-c clusters, and iterate on prefix-cache sizing.
- Goal: reduce token-cost spikes from sudden bursty traffic and avoid cold-start autoscale pauses at 02:00–03:30 PST.

Top-of-shift quick checks (15m)
- /check nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu  # look for NotReady or taints
- grafana: gpu-pool-overview -> check 99th latency, eviction rate panels
- slack: #infra-ops for any overnight alerts (scan pinned)
- cloud console: list preemptible events for last 6h (gcloud compute operations list)

Immediate TODOs (ordered)
[ ] 1) Finish N2 drift rebalancing (target clusters: n2-c-7, n2-c-8)
    - short plan: cordon one node in n2-c-7, drain low-priority pods, restart runtime-agent, uncordon 
    - note: watch node-exporter cpu spikes after restart (was seen on 2026-02-27)
    - estimated 30m, risk: transient 50–200ms tail increase for ongoing requests

[ ] 2) Prefix cache sizing experiment for embed-heavy routes
    - current: 384MB per pod prefix cache; hypothesis: 512MB reduces downstream token calls by ~18% for small-session workloads
    - experiment: bump cache to 512MB on two canary hosts in region us-west2 for 4 hours, collect cache hit-rate and token-per-request metrics
    - commands: set CONFIG_PREFIX_CACHE=512 && rollout restart deploy/realtime-runtime-canary

[ ] 3) Networking: validate egress SNAT pool exhaustion alerts
    - symptom: intermittent 504s to third-party auth when burst > 1k conn/min
    - quick check: sudo ss -s on proxy boxes; look for high TIME_WAIT counts
    - mitigation: increase SNAT ephemeral port range on hosts + add one NAT gateway to us-west2-b

[ ] 4) Follow-up tickets (low time): triage INFRA-1287 and ENGOPS-342 (see linked artifacts)

Notes to self — Observations & quick wins:
- Autoscaler cooldown currently at 120s; consider 60s for small bursty routes (tradeoff with noisy scaling). Put a short doc in /confluence proposing 60s for routes with p50 < 60ms.
- Seen 2x higher cold-start p99 on gpu-quant models when sequence_len > 1024; may be kernel selection fallback issue. Flag for runtime team.
- For tonight, prefer conservative quant_pack config to avoid OOMs during packing (pack_size=8 instead of 12).

Commands & snippets I actually use (paste-ready)
- kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node> --grace-period=60
- gcloud compute instances describe <node> --project redwood-prod --zone us-west2-b --format=json | jq '.status'
- ssh ops@proxy-usw2-03 "sudo ss -s | head -n 20"

Small capacity math (ballpark)
- current running GPU pods in us-west2: 138 pods (avg util 64%)
- expected holiday burst: +22% peak token-rate -> need ~30 extra pods to keep p95 latency steady
- reserved buffer: maintain 12% spare headroom (~17 pods) before triggering provisioning bump request

Parking lot / follow-ups (not urgent)
- write quick howto for canary cache bump experiment (template)
- propose a cross-team postmortem template for transient networking 504s
- test sysctl tweaks for TIME_WAIT reuse during low-traffic hours

Questions for morning stand / handoff
- Did the canary cache bump alter blacklist false-positive rate for rerank service? (ask Aisha)
- Confirm with SRE if decreasing autoscaler cooldown to 60s will impact global cluster churn metrics (ask Marcus)

Last 10-minute checklist before handoff
- update INFRA-1287 with observations + logs
- post brief summary to #infra-shift-handoff: what I ran, what I changed, what to watch
- leave sticky note on board: "do not change pack_size for quant models until 2026-03-15"

Random notes-to-self (raw)
- If node-exporter spikes after drain, check kernel dmesg for CPU steal and cgroups throttling
- Keep an eye on persistent disk IO latency in b instances (slow DB ops lead to pipeline backups)

End of notebook — keep concise, iterate, ship small experiments.
